hypothesis: If the claim holds, cuttlefishes (Sepiidae) are described as having an internal cuttlebone (os sepiae), squids (calamaries) as having a gladius (pen), and octopuses (poulps) as having no such internal shell.
pass_criterion: Supports if all three group clauses match. Sepiidae matches if the FAO catalogue text places a cuttlebone or sepion in Sepiidae and does not say that Sepiidae lack one. Squids match if the FAO squid catalogue places a gladius or pen in squids (Loliginidae, Myopsida, or Oegopsida) as a possessed structure. Octopuses match only if the FAO octopod catalogue says the internal shell, gladius, cuttlebone, and shell vestige or stylet are absent in Octopoda or Incirrata as a group. A vestige counts as an internal hard part: stylets, a vestigial gladius, or a shell vestige stated as present means the octopus clause does not match.
fail_criterion: A clause fails if the catalogue states the opposite: Sepiidae without a cuttlebone, squids without a gladius, or octopuses with a cuttlebone, gladius, or shell vestige or stylet. Refutes if two or three clauses fail. Mixed if exactly one clause fails, or if a group is described as variable (present in some, absent in others), which fails a universal wording for that group. Inconclusive, reason data-unavailable, if a PDF cannot be downloaded or if two or more groups have no explicit shell sentence (no co-occurrence, inside one paragraph or an 800-character window, of the group name and a shell term). The short body-sac explanation is not tested.

test_contract.expected_observation: FAO diagnoses or keys state a cuttlebone in Sepiidae, a gladius in squids, and no internal shell or shell vestige in octopuses.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: The same catalogues deny a cuttlebone in Sepiidae, deny a gladius in squids, or attribute an internal shell, gladius, or stylet or shell vestige to octopuses.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: The three open FAO species-catalogue PDFs named in planned_datasets, text-extracted by the script. Family and order names must occur in the same paragraph or within 800 characters of the shell term. A figure caption that only labels a drawing is not used unless it states presence or absence. Nautiluses and sepiolids are outside the three clauses: Sepiidae is the cuttlefish clause, not every sepioid.
test_contract.inference_method: Extract text, find windows that join each group name to cuttlebone, sepion, gladius, pen, stylet, or shell vestige, and code presence or absence from the negation in that window ('absent', 'without', 'lacking', 'no '). Then apply the three-clause rule. Confidence is 0.70 if supports, 0.65 if refutes, 0.50 if mixed, and 0.55 if inconclusive.

interpretation: Cuttle-fishes are Sepiidae, calamaries are the squids covered by the FAO squid volume (myopsid and oegopsid squids, including Loliginidae), and poulps are octopods. The claim says octopuses have no internal part of the sort just named (os sepiae, gladius). A stylet or shell vestige is that sort of part, reduced. The claim's reason, a short body-sac, is not measured.
caveats: A web search displayed a short FAO key excerpt on sepioid shells before this file was committed. The pass and fail rules were written from the claim, not edited to fit that excerpt. The three catalogue PDFs were not downloaded before this commit.
Group-level sentences in a catalogue are not a species-by-species census. A match shows what the catalogue asserts about the group.
